About the field

Who is researching the Indus civilisation, and on what

Everyone who published on the Indus civilisation, its script and its neighbours in the past year, grouped into research directions, with the leading groups and the papers to read. For the newest papers and our checks of them, see News.

01The field

The field now: who is working on what

Roughly 420 researchers published on the Indus civilisation, its script and its neighbours in the past year, across these 8 directions.

Past 12 months, updated 19 November 2026. Bars show distinct authors; lines show papers per year (the dashed end is this year so far). These are estimates from keyword matches, not a census.

How we counted

Counts are estimates from keyword matches in OpenAlex titles and abstracts (journal articles, reviews and book chapters; self-archived preprints left out because they include many unreviewed decipherment claims), for the 12 months to the update date. A paper can match more than one direction, and the headline removes people counted twice. Distinct authors and institutions are exact up to 400 papers per direction and extrapolated from the newest 400 above that. Each direction lists its exact query so anyone can check it.

  1. 1Excavation and site archaeology

    Dig and date the cities, towns and villages to learn how the civilisation lived, grew and ended.

    ~200 authors · ~90 papers · ~100 institutions

    20212026

    rising+21% a year, 2021–2025

    Leading groupsVikrant Jain (IIT Gandhinagar) · V. N. Prabhakar (IIT Gandhinagar) · Prabodh Shirvalkar (Deccan College) · Yadubirsingh Rawat (Archaeological Survey of India) · Heather M.-L. Miller (University of Toronto) · Cameron A. Petrie (University of Cambridge)

    NowNew digs at Rakhigarhi, the waterways around Dholavira, and old spy-satellite images used to track threatened mounds. Read: Gupta VK 2026, Chatterjee A 2026, Gerrits PJ 2026.

    Query

    (Harappan OR "Indus Civilization" OR "Indus civilisation" OR "Indus Valley Civilization" OR "Indus Valley Civilisation") AND (excavation OR site OR settlement OR archaeological)

    Filter: type:article|review|book-chapter,primary_location.source.type:journal|book series|ebook platform|conference, published 2025-11-20 to 2026-11-19. Check the count on OpenAlex (the meta.count field).

  2. 2Climate and rivers

    Changing monsoons and shifting rivers shaped where Harappans lived and why the cities emptied.

    ~110 authors · ~40 papers · ~50 institutions

    20212026

    rising+16% a year, 2021–2025

    Leading groupsCameron A. Petrie (University of Cambridge) · David A. Hodell (University of Cambridge) · Yama Dixit (IIT Delhi) · Vikrant Jain (IIT Gandhinagar) · Siddharth P. Prizomwala (Institute of Seismological Research)

    NowSome now argue that drying rivers, and not only a weaker monsoon, drove the late Harappan change. Lost channels of the Sutlej and Ghaggar are being remapped. Read: Solanki H 2025, Shekhar S 2026, Chatterjee A 2026.

    Query

    (Harappan OR "Indus Civilization" OR "Indus civilisation" OR "Indus Valley Civilization" OR "Indus Valley Civilisation") AND (climate OR monsoon OR river OR rivers OR drought OR palaeoclimate OR paleoclimate OR Holocene)

    Filter: type:article|review|book-chapter,primary_location.source.type:journal|book series|ebook platform|conference, published 2025-11-20 to 2026-11-19. Check the count on OpenAlex (the meta.count field).

  3. 3Crafts, materials and isotopes

    Beads, metal, pottery, bones and residues, measured in the lab, show how goods were made and how people ate and moved.

    ~110 authors · ~40 papers · ~60 institutions

    20212026

    rising+35% a year, 2021–2025

    Leading groupsCameron A. Petrie (University of Cambridge) · V. N. Prabhakar (IIT Gandhinagar) · Yadubirsingh Rawat (Archaeological Survey of India) · Anil Kumar Pokharia (Birbal Sahni Institute of Palaeosciences) · Heather M.-L. Miller (University of Toronto)

    NowStudies of pottery, beads and stone tools ask how stable Harappan craft methods were and where the raw materials came from. Read: Sarkar S 2026, Mahala MK 2025, Gadekar C 2025.

    Query

    (Harappan OR "Indus Civilization" OR "Indus civilisation" OR "Indus Valley Civilization" OR "Indus Valley Civilisation") AND (bead OR beads OR isotope OR isotopic OR residue OR ceramic OR pottery OR metallurgy OR copper OR faunal OR archaeobotanical)

    Filter: type:article|review|book-chapter,primary_location.source.type:journal|book series|ebook platform|conference, published 2025-11-20 to 2026-11-19. Check the count on OpenAlex (the meta.count field).

  4. 4Trade and Meluhha

    Harappan goods and seals abroad, and Meluhha in Mesopotamian texts, map the long-distance links.

    ~100 authors · ~40 papers · ~50 institutions

    20212026

    rising+22% a year, 2021–2025

    Leading groupsV. N. Prabhakar (IIT Gandhinagar) · Vikrant Jain (IIT Gandhinagar) · Cameron A. Petrie (University of Cambridge) · Michel de Vreeze (Durham University)

    NowRiver wharves, Umm an-Nar sites in Oman, and a reported seal with Indus signs from the UAE are filling in the river and sea routes. Read: Hakal M 2026, Douglas KA 2026, News report 2026.

    Query

    Meluhha OR ((Harappan OR "Indus Civilization" OR "Indus civilisation" OR "Indus Valley Civilization" OR "Indus Valley Civilisation") AND (Mesopotamia OR Mesopotamian OR Gulf OR Oman OR Dilmun OR Magan OR trade OR exchange))

    Filter: type:article|review|book-chapter,primary_location.source.type:journal|book series|ebook platform|conference, published 2025-11-20 to 2026-11-19. Check the count on OpenAlex (the meta.count field).

  5. 5Ancient DNA

    Genomes from skeletons show who the Harappans were descended from and who descended from them.

    ~80 authors · ~13 papers · ~50 institutions

    20212026

    steady-2% a year, 2021–2025

    Leading groupsNiraj Rai (Birbal Sahni Institute of Palaeosciences) · David Reich (Broad Institute) · Gyaneshwer Chaubey (Banaras Hindu University) · Mohammed Shafiul Mustak (Mangalore University)

    NowOnly one Harappan genome has been published (Rakhigarhi, 2019). Newer work reads ancestry from living groups such as the Nilgiri and Koraga tribes. Read: Shinde et al.; Narasimhan et al. 2019, Desai S 2026, Sequeira JJ 2025.

    Query

    ("ancient DNA" OR "ancient genomes" OR "ancient genome" OR archaeogenetic OR archaeogenomic OR paleogenomic OR palaeogenomic) AND ("South Asia" OR India OR Pakistan OR Harappan OR Indus)

    Filter: type:article|review|book-chapter,primary_location.source.type:journal|book series|ebook platform|conference, published 2025-11-20 to 2026-11-19. Check the count on OpenAlex (the meta.count field).

  6. 6Undeciphered scripts in general

    Methods tried on Linear A, Proto-Elamite, rongorongo and others carry over to the Indus script, and the reverse.

    ~80 authors · ~40 papers · ~40 institutions

    20212026

    rising+10% a year, 2021–2025

    Leading groupsBrent Davis (University of Melbourne) · Silvia Ferrara (University of Bologna) · Jacob L. Dahl (University of Oxford) · Miguel Valério (University of Oxford)

    NowLinear Elamite has a claimed decipherment that is being tested on new texts. Aegean, rongorongo and Voynich work is turning to calibrated statistical tests. Read: Desset 2022, Davis 2026, Zhang 2026.

    UsOur ‘is it language’ tests, with fair synthetic controls, apply to these scripts as much as to the Indus signs.

    Query

    "undeciphered script" OR "undeciphered scripts" OR "undeciphered writing" OR rongorongo OR "Proto-Elamite" OR "Linear Elamite" OR "Cretan hieroglyphic" OR "Cypro-Minoan" OR "Voynich manuscript" OR "Indus script" OR "Linear A script"

    Filter: type:article|review|book-chapter,primary_location.source.type:journal|book series|ebook platform|conference, published 2025-11-20 to 2026-11-19. Check the count on OpenAlex (the meta.count field).

  7. 7The language question

    Which language family the Harappans spoke (Dravidian, Munda, a lost language or another) decides how any reading could work.

    ~50 authors · ~19 papers · ~20 institutions

    20212026

    rising+27% a year, 2021–2025

    Leading groupsMohammed Shafiul Mustak (Mangalore University) · Jaison Jeevan Sequeira (Mangalore University) · George van Driem (University of Bern) · Gyaneshwer Chaubey (Banaras Hindu University)

    NowGenetics of Dravidian-speaking groups and a Bayesian tree of the Dravidian family are the main new evidence on what the Harappans spoke. Read: Sequeira JJ 2025, Narayan S 2025, Kolipakam V 2018.

    UsOur mismatch study uses planted ciphers to test how decipherment methods fail when the guessed language is wrong.

    Query

    (Harappan OR "Indus Civilization" OR "Indus civilisation" OR "Indus Valley Civilization" OR "Indus script") AND (Dravidian OR "Proto-Dravidian" OR Munda OR "Indo-Aryan" OR "Indo-European" OR "language family" OR linguistic)

    Filter: type:article|review|book-chapter,primary_location.source.type:journal|book series|ebook platform|conference, published 2025-11-20 to 2026-11-19. Check the count on OpenAlex (the meta.count field).

  8. 8Indus script studies

    Work out what the signs are and how the inscriptions are built, from sign lists, structure and statistics.

    ~20 authors · ~16 papers · ~12 institutions

    20212026

    rising+36% a year, 2021–2025

    Leading groupsDebasis Mitra (Florida Institute of Technology) · Ujjwal Bhattacharya (Indian Statistical Institute) · Gregg M. Jamison (University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee) · Yuji Yamaguchi (Okayama University)

    NowNo lab-scale group works on the script. The output is mostly single-author proposals of readings, plus a few statistical and deep-learning papers on signs and seals. Read: Kriger 2026, Dominik 2026, Dixit 2025.

    UsOur restoration bench found that models do not beat simple sign-sequence counts once near-copies are excluded.

    Query

    "Indus script" OR "Harappan script" OR "Indus inscriptions" OR "Indus signs" OR "Indus seals" OR "Harappan seals"

    Filter: type:article|review|book-chapter,primary_location.source.type:journal|book series|ebook platform|conference, published 2025-11-20 to 2026-11-19. Check the count on OpenAlex (the meta.count field).
